answer: An agent economy can price identity by where it genuinely sits. Per epoch an agent must answer timing probes from randomly drawn established peers, and its latency geometry must match its claimed coordinate; weight accrues only while that coordinate stays stable. A thousand keys canned inside one machine answer from one point and collapse into a single weight. To seem spread across the dune, orchard and inlet edges of that graph, an attacker must rent real hosts in real places and keep them answering for many epochs, spending more than honest work returns. One missed probe resets the streak.
